title: --max-cost-usd is an inert cap: every provider adapter reports costUsd: 0, so a cost-only cap never trips and the run is unbounded
evidence: packages/ai/src/providers/ollama.ts:93 and gemini.ts:85 both return costUsd: 0; llm-eval.mjs createLlmScoreFn sums r.costUsd and checks stats.costUsd >= caps.maxCostUsd, which is never true. parseLlmArgs accepts '--llm --model m --max-cost-usd 5' as a valid cap. The only tested cost-cap case uses a fake complete returning costUsd 0.4.
fix_direction: Refuse (exit 2) a cost-only cap unless --max-calls is also given, or estimate cost from tokens with a stated per-model rate; add a test that parseLlmArgs rejects --max-cost-usd alone for providers that report 0 cost; add a boundary test for costUsd === maxCostUsd (mutation 'costUsd > maxCostUsd' survives today).

title: cost cap is checked-then-spent without reservation, so concurrent callers could overshoot by the in-flight count; call cap is safe (calls++ is synchronous)
evidence: scoreFn checks stats.costUsd before the await; current callers (calibrateLlm, rankSessionsLlm) are serial so no overshoot today.
fix_direction: note only; reserve before await if concurrency is ever added.
